title: sideband: hub-initiated remove and ban of a user in a hosted room
description: The hub, as external sender, sends a Remove proposal for the user's leaves plus the participant_list update (ban: role 1). Needs an external-proposal path in the hub; write a design note first. Point 3d.
design:
DRAFT 2026-11-15, needs Mark: conflicts with approved decision mimid-1wgh.6.46 (hub sends no external proposals in v1).

How it would work. The hub is each hosted room's MLS external sender (external_senders names it). For POST /local/v1/rooms/{roomId}/remove {user} (ban: {user, ban: true}) the hub:
1. signs, as that external sender, a Remove proposal for each of the user's leaves and an AppDataUpdate for participant_list removing the user (ban: changing their role to 1, banned);
2. records them as the room's pending proposals, so the next Commit must include them (decision mimid-1wgh.6.5, already enforced);
3. fans them out to the members as a proposal bundle.
The hub cannot commit (it is not a member). The removal takes effect when any member commits; until then the user is still a member. Each step logs at INFO.

New pieces: mimi-mls Observer::propose_remove (external Remove; Observer::propose_app_data_update exists already); hub policy accepts the hub's own external proposals (still refuses every other external sender); a fanout of hub proposals.

Policy question: room-policy has no operator role, so a hub removal overrides the room's own policy (who may kick or ban). That is an operator power outside the drafts; say so in the docs.

Decision needed: amend mimid-1wgh.6.46 to let the hub send its own Remove and participant_list proposals for operator remove and ban, or drop .47.5.
